candidates.title: Set and lock a robot gripper opening stop, then verify retained motion
candidates.objective: On an unpressurized, already-assembled representative SCHUNK DRG 80 bench fixture, adjust the opening-stop screw to a declared 90° total opening, lock it without changing the setting, withdraw both tools, and operate a cold test lever to verify retained opening over repeated cycles.
skills: open-ended wrench seating on a thin jam nut
coupled screw adjustment and nut locking
candidates.success_conditions: Initial score is 0. Award 0.25 for a released opening within 6° of the declared 90° target; 0.5 when within 3° with nut 73 seated against the cover and nut 74 retained in its modeled installed position; 0.75 when both tools are removed and one close-open cycle returns within 3°; 1.0 after three cycles each return within 3°, stop drift is at most 2°, both nuts remain retained, and tools and robot grippers remain at least 30 mm clear for one second. Revoke angle and cycle credit whenever locking, retention, or clearance prerequisites fail. A missing screw or nut, a dropped or inaccessible tool, fixture displacement, non-finite state, or a configured maximum-opening setting outside the modeled 20°–180° adjustment range, or a violation of the fixture's actual mechanical limits, scores 0. Ordinary closing below 20° during functional cycles is permitted. Equivalent safe strategies earn the same outcome score; arm identity, order, path, action count, and impulse windows are not graded. The target, tolerances, cycle count, and clearance are explicit benchmark assumptions checkable by protractor, witness marks, nut-gap inspection, and video.
candidates.industrial_value: SCHUNK specifies opening-angle adjustment, locking, and pneumatic functional testing for its DRG 44–80 industrial grippers, making this direct robot-end-effector setup work within Impact on AI timelines. Its tested ability differs from generic tightening and the accepted hose-clamp task: the robot must preserve an adjustable stop against locknut reaction and then demonstrate hands-off functional retention. It also differs from PR 1540 because two concentric tools act on a coupled screw-and-nut setting rather than stabilizing a sensor body during connector assembly, and from PR 2229 because no third-body feeler gauge or cam clamp establishes the target.
candidates.dexterity: One gripper must keep a driver seated in the adjustment screw while the other seats and turns a wrench on nut 73. Tightening must physically tend to disturb an unrestrained screw, requiring coordinated countertorque, angular regulation, possible wrench regrasping, clean tool withdrawal, and subsequent operation of the articulated test fixture.

candidates.asset_plan: Build independently authored, full-scale representative rigid geometry, not a redistributed SCHUNK CAD model. Preserve the catalog drawing’s dimensional semantics: 100 × 71.6 × 135.5 mm are catalog X/Y/Z reference dimensions, not a claimed bounding envelope, and the page-7 drawing separately shows a 183.35 mm extent to point P. Represent the anodized-aluminum housing, steel angular jaws, native revolute jaw joints, common centric coupling, accessible adjustment screw, nut 73 as the locking nut, and retained nut 74 as the second manufacturer-specified nut; its precise spacing and role beyond installation are disclosed fixture assumptions because the manual does not explain them. Provide real hex and wrench contact geometry and a native or conservative task-local torque/friction mechanism in which tightening disturbs an unrestrained screw. The cold lever replaces pneumatic actuation only for bench verification. Target angle, hardware dimensions absent from the manual, friction, preload, and tolerances remain declared assumptions. Before demo development, validate reset, tool seating, restrained-versus-unrestrained causality, joint traces, loss cases, release clearance, and timestep sensitivity in the pinned Isaac Sim 6.1/YAM runtime.
candidates.risk: Closest ability-level neighbors include PR 1540, PR 1799, PR 1865, PR 2018, PR 2167, and PR 2229. Novelty depends on retaining genuine concentric two-tool screw/nut countertorque and functional-cycle verification; an implementation with zero driver reaction or a scripted phase flag would collapse into existing stabilization or adjustment tasks. No current native gripper trial exists, so implementation feasibility and physics validation remain future gates rather than claimed evidence.

candidates.title: Calibrate a DRG 80 inductive endpoint switch and verify switching
candidates.objective: Position the DRG 80 open-position proximity-switch bracket against its control cam, establish the specified approximately 0.5 mm setback, fasten the bracket, and cycle the gripper to verify reliable endpoint switching.
candidates.success_conditions: Partial credit would require the sensor seated in its bracket and the bracket brought to the cam without collision. Higher credit would require a released 0.5 mm setback within a declared tolerance and retained fasteners. Full credit would require correct switching through repeated open-close cycles with the robot clear. Bracket or sensor loss, cam collision, unsafe overtravel, false switching, or loss of the setback would revoke affected credit.
candidates.industrial_value: The SCHUNK manual specifies this endpoint-sensor calibration for DRG grippers, so it is genuine end-effector commissioning. However, its central ability—setting a proximity-sensor gap, locking it, and functionally checking it—substantially overlaps PR 2229.
candidates.dexterity: The robot would position a small sensor and movable bracket, establish a fine physical setback from a cam, preserve it while tightening, and validate the result through articulated cycles.

Drive a visible indicator only from measured sensor-to-cam separation. Treat missing sensor and bracket dimensions as explicit fixture assumptions.
candidates.risk: PR 2229 already tests positioning a proximity sensor to a measured gap, locking it, withdrawing the gauge, and checking the released result. Different hardware, a 0.5 mm setback, and screw rather than cam locking do not establish a distinct tested ability. Exact IN 80 and bracket geometry is also unavailable in the acquired evidence.
missing_evidence: A defensible ability-level novelty distinction from PR 2229
Authoritative or independently measured IN 80 sensor and bracket geometry

candidates.title: Compress and secure a DRG 80 spring-loaded piston with its assembly device
candidates.objective: During DRG 80 maintenance, place the cylinder piston over its springs, align the manufacturer-style assembly device and locating pin, compress and secure the loaded stack, tighten the piston screw, remove the device, and verify installation position.
candidates.success_conditions: Partial credit would cover correct spring and piston placement and seating of the assembly device and locating pin. Higher credit would require controlled compression with all parts retained and fixture screws seated. Full credit would require the piston screw secured, device removed without ejection, installation position verified, and all tools released. A spring, piston, screw, fixture, or tool leaving the work area, uncontrolled release, fixture displacement, or misalignment would score 0.
candidates.industrial_value: SCHUNK explicitly prescribes an assembly device for servicing DRG 44–100 grippers. The operation is meaningful robot-end-effector maintenance and tests alignment plus fastener work while controlling stored spring energy.
candidates.dexterity: The robot must align constrained parts while sustaining compressive load, insert and turn fasteners without losing the stack, and unload the fixture gradually. This demands genuine bimanual force control rather than ordinary placement.

A safe full-scale fixture arrangement reachable by both YAM arms

selection_reason: The opening-stop task is the only candidate with a complete manufacturer procedure, supported DRG 80 external geometry and materials, a known screw-and-two-nut mechanism, a rigid full-scale asset path, and no critical evidence gap. The repaired plan preserves the catalog drawing’s reference-dimension semantics, explicitly includes nut 74, and uses short extraction-clean quotations. Its distinct tested ability is maintaining a coupled angular stop with two simultaneously seated tools against locknut reaction, followed by hands-off functional-cycle retention. The sensor candidate is blocked by direct ability overlap, while the piston candidate lacks essential internal geometry and spring-force evidence.
